articles.title: Kelly Krauskopf stepping down as Indiana Fever team president
articles.summary: Krauskopf started with Pacers Sports & Entertainment in 1999.
articles.body:
Kelly Krauskopf, who has served as president of basketball and business operations for the Indiana Fever since 2024, announced Friday that she is stepping down from her role.

"It has been an honor and a privilege to help build and steward the Indiana Fever with the support and trust of Herb Simon," Krauskopf said in a statement. "I am deeply grateful for the opportunities, relationships, and shared accomplishments that have shaped my time with this organization. The Fever is poised for an exciting future, and I am proud to have helped lay the foundation for its continued growth and success. I will always cherish my time with Pacers Sports and Entertainment and the people who made it so meaningful."

The 64-year-old has been part of Pacers Sports & Entertainment since 1999 when the Fever joined the WNBA. As the team's president and general manager until 2017, she helped the franchise make 13 playoff appearances and three WNBA Finals berths, which included a title in 2012.

In 2018, Krauskopf was named assistant GM of the Indiana Pacers and became the first woman to hold an executive basketball management role in NBA history.

After six years on the NBA side of the organization, Krauskopf returned to the Fever as president of basketball and business operations in 2024. One year later, the team reached the WNBA semifinals. In 2026, they were back in the postseason and improved their win total for the fourth straight season.

After her collegiate playing career at Texas A&M, Krauskopf was assistant commissioner of the Southwest Conference before joining the WNBA as the league's first director of operations when it started in 1996 . She has also been a part of three USA Basketball women's national team selection committees for multiple Olympic cycles.

articles.title: Why the Hawks are a rare NBA road favorite worth backing against the rebuilding Hornets
articles.summary: The Atlanta Hawks face the Charlotte Hornets with Jalen Johnson leading a revamped roster, while Brandon Miller tries to carry a depleted squad.
articles.body: The NBA is just a few days old and we've already seen two teams blow 20-point leads. That happens more often than you'd probably imagine, and this year I'm making a point to live bet on the team that is losing big. Last night the 76ers looked awful, but they came back in the second half of the game and covered the short spread. I'm sure it will happen somewhere today as well. There are a ton of great games to choose from, but I've got my eye on the Hawks and Hornets game. The Atlanta Hawks are one of the teams that have a bit of excitement behind them coming into this year. They revamped their roster quite a bit over the past few years, but now it seems like they have decided to build their team around Jalen Johnson. It also helps that they have two really good defenders - Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels. The team moved on from Trae Young last year, who was a facilitator and scorer for them, but also a parking cone on defense, and it never seemed like the team worked with him. This team is now a little more athletic and younger, but still grounded with a couple of key veterans like CJ McCollum. In their opening game against the Magic, I was most impressed with their shot selection. As a team, they shot 50% from the field and 40% from deep. You really can't expect that to happen consistently, but they did create the good shots. Defensively, they really weren't impressive. They still gave up 125 points to the Magic, which is a lot for an Orlando team that isn't known for being offensively efficient. The Charlotte Hornets remain one of those teams that I really can't understand. They have been terrible for years, and the one time they sniffed success, they decided it was time to trade away their (arguably) best player. They sent LaMelo Ball over to the Timberwolves, but that's probably because they have Coby White, and they seem to want to invest in Kon Knueppel. Unfortunately for them, Knueppel is out with an injury right now, so the team is missing a major player. In their first game, they unveiled their new-look roster and beat the Brooklyn Nets on the road. This team is comprised of multiple role players, but right now, their biggest semblance of a star is Brandon Miller. No offense to Miller, but if he is responsible for leading the team for multiple games, you're probably asking for trouble. I do think the Hornets are going to be hovering around the play-in positioning for the postseason, but I really don't think they've improved from last year. I really don't enjoy taking favorites on the road in the NBA. Role players don't play as well on the road as they do at home, but in this one, I'm willing to make an exception. The Hawks are the better team, have a better offense, and I think they should win this one. They do play at home tomorrow, against a tougher opponent, so this could be a trap spot, but I'm going to take them on the moneyline at -135. I do think they know how to win, and I think the Hornets are trying to figure things out. articles.title: ‘Getting a ring before Luka ‘ – NBA Fans excited for Dalton Knecht as he signs two-way contract with New York Knicks
articles.summary: Former LA Lakers player Dalton Knecht has found a new home as the New York Knicks signed him to a two-way contract just days after the Purple and Gold outfit...
articles.body:
Former LA Lakers player Dalton Knecht has found a new home as the New York Knicks signed him to a two-way contract just days after the Purple and Gold outfit waived him.

The former Tennessee player was the 17th pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. He had a solid rookie season, but after a poor second year and a disappointing preseason, the Lakers decided to waive him from their final roster.

However, just days later, Knecht has been picked by the Knicks, who waived Kevin McCullar Jr. to make room for the former Lakers player.

McCullar was one of the players on the Knicks roster who was given the ring on opening night. He had impressive performances for the team, but the franchise decided to give Knecht a chance to prove his talent to the rest of the league.

In the preseason, Knecht scored 11 points against the Golden State Warriors in one game and went scoreless in two others. His form has been in decline since the Lakers decided to trade him away, and a deal was even in place with the Charlotte Hornets. But after it collapsed due to Mark Williams' failed medical, Knecht had to return to Los Angeles.

After that debacle, he has failed to find himself, which is why a change in environment could prove to be massive for him.

Fans react to Dalton Knecht signing with the New York Knicks

Knecht had a top rookie season. In a game against the Utah Jazz, he scored 37 points, draining 9 three-pointers, a record for a rookie in the NBA.

Despite his performances, the team included him in a trade package for Mark Williams; from then on, he failed to replicate the talent that was on display until February of 2025.

There is evidence that Knecht is a tremendous shooter. While it has not been on display in a long time, the Knicks are playing a gamble that can be fruitful.

Fans were excited to hear that the team had added another promising talent to the roster.

"Dalton getting a ring before Luka," said one fan. An account named Real App on X added: "Knicks going back-to-back confirmed."

Someone also stated: "Let shooters shoot……. We are wishing the best for this ex Laker."

"This is a good swing for a player with shooting upside. If it works out, Knicks get an elite shooter. If it doesn't, who cares. Good buy low from the Knicks," a fan opined.

An account user remarked: "Good luck Dalton! Hopefully getting recruited by the champs is the confidence boost he needs."

Knecht has a chance to do something special with the Knicks and even convert his two-way into a standard NBA contract. The team has a lot of special players who are selfless. He will have to adapt to this, as it is the only way he can succeed in the organisation.
